newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds see ICI pep up the sterling sector.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds see ICI pep up the sterling sector.

text.p: ICI launched its second Eurobond in as many weeks on Wednesday, enlivening what was an otherwise routine session.

Banks involved reported good demand for the ICI transaction -- a 300 million stg 10-year launched on the back of a prior well-received dollar deal -- and said it had tightened to 69 67 basis points from the 70 b.p. reoffer level.
"ICI is keen to establish benchmark bonds in key markets. This benchmark in its home market is a followthrough from the success of the dollar deal," a syndicate manager close to the deal said.
While British funds were the main buyers, the level of German, Swiss and, to a lesser extent, Asian money for the deal was unexpectedly high, bankers said.
BZW and NatWest Markets were joint lead managers.

ICI on July 22 issued a $500 million five-year Eurobond, its first public offering in international capital markets since it floated off Zeneca in 1993. That deal has tightened to 48.0 46.5 b.p. from its 50 b.p. launch spread.
Proceeds from both bonds will go towards the refinancing of an $8.5 billion loan ICI took out in May in conjunction with its $8 billion purchase of Unilever's speciality chemicals business.
ICI went some way to reducing that bill earlier this month when it sold half its bulk chemical operations to U.S. chemicals giant DuPont for $3 billion.
ICI is rated Baa1 by Moody's and A- by S&P, having been cut from A3 in June and A+ in May respectively after the Unilever purchase.
Elsewhere, Yapi Kredi, the largest private bank in Turkey, made its Euromarket debut with a $150 million five-year financing at a 395 b.p. spread over U.S. Treasuries. UBS was lead manager.
